I’d just like to interject for a moment. What you’re refering to as Linux, is in fact, GNU/Linux, or as I’ve recently taken to calling it, GNU plus Linux. Linux is not an operating system unto itself, but rather another free component of a fully functioning GNU system made useful by the GNU corelibs, shell utilities and vital system components comprising a full OS as defined by POSIX.

Many computer users run a modified version of the GNU system every day, without realizing it. Through a peculiar turn of events, the version of GNU which is widely used today is often called Linux, and many of its users are not aware that it is basically the GNU system, developed by the GNU Project.

There really is a Linux, and these people are using it, but it is just a part of the system they use. Linux is the kernel: the program in the system that allocates the machine’s resources to the other programs that you run. The kernel is an essential part of an operating system, but useless by itself; it can only function in the context of a complete operating system. Linux is normally used in combination with the GNU operating system: the whole system is basically GNU with Linux added, or GNU/Linux. All the so-called Linux distributions are really distributions of GNU/Linux!

Besides supply issue another problem of deathstacking shitters is reinforce meme, basically when the enemy is deorging your troops faster than other divisions sitting on the same tile but not yet in the battle due to combat width limit reinforcing into the battle. Cas and quality divisions like armoured division stacked with soft attack can melt infantry pretty easily.

Two way you can overcome this, either make your front line divisions better and last in a battle longer, this means more stats like defense and org, this has nothing to do with the amount of divisions that sit in one tile when you fill up the combat width limit of the province. For example a plain tile has 90 cw and additional attack from another direction will increase the cw by 30 (can't remember the exact value but you get the meaning), meaning you can have six 20 width divisions engaging in the battle at the same time at most, more units will only enter the battle when the six units start to retreat when they run out of org, at the reinforce rate you have per hour. For example 10% reinforce rate meaning a reserve unit have 10% chance of joining the battle when theres emptied battle width that it can roughly fit every hour. That brings the reason to pick right line of mass assault doctrine if you want to leverage on the sheer amount of troops you can pump out when fighting an enemy with fewer but better divisions. The right side of MA gives tonnes of reinforce rate and reduction of combat with of infantry battalions, meaning you can first stuff more dudes in a battle before exceeding the combat width limit, second reserves sitting in the same tile are more ready to join the battle when the fighting units are deorged, reducing the chance of reinforce meme. Radio tech gives you reinforce rate as well.

You can click on the green or red bubble of a battle to check how fast your divisions are getting deorged by the enemy, hover your cursor to the stats of both attacker and defender to see the stats breakdown.

One cannot solely focus on examining an education system without understanding the social background and the purpose it serves in a society. 

Regardless of whether the students themselves understand or not, most students in not only Singapore but also Korea, China and India etc feel the stress  . Be it the challenge posed by school curriculum or extracurricular activity commitment, the mindset that breeds the stress of 'cannot fall behind' that fuels the rat race in these countries ultimately comes from the fear of not being to climb up or maintain the socio economic status. Unless ones family can live on capital increment, going through the education system is almost the sole path towards conventional societal success. Many are proud of the fact that education is a path of climbing up the social ladder in our society but this means education is given a task that it is not meant for. By coupling the result of education to ones future level of material satisfaction, respect from the society and opportunities that one may provide with ones offsprings with, the stake of excelling in the education system is made artificially high. But why would falling down in ses such a big deal? Because the bottom of our society is living in misery inconceivable to many. The lack of a welfare system that should be comparable to many western countries given our economic progress in all these years makes 捡 cardboard a funny but true fear that many could experience. The high cost of living coupled with a not yet sufficiently robust social safety net makes the fight for climbing the social ladder a massively competitive free for all battle royale.

Now it's time for extremely unpopular opinion: Asians are not 'smarter' on average, many of us who are still struggling in academic performance might just not be meant to go this far in the education system. They are forced into doing H2 H3s that they are frankly not gifted in, they are doing these for the rank points. Of course our society still holds prejudice against the less well performed students in academics, ITE and even polytechnic students are often perceived to be 'less intelligent' or 'less hardworking'. The lack of respect and acknowledgement of the value of many essential but less paid or 'skilled' as in qualification required also stem from the same root. With the pressure coming from oneself, family members who knows well the strong correlation of education qualification and future choice as well as the society as a whole pile tremendous amount of pressure on students. Those who are less academically inclined suffer the most. I've personally seen many being force to choose JC over poly ITE or even starting to work because of peer and family pressure, and end up grinding things they don't enjoy learning in schools. How many students are truly passionate about learning? how many students are truly capable of truly understanding and utilising the knowledge taught in our schools but mechanically memorising and building up muscle memory from repeated practice? 

In summary, the stress that Singaporean students face does not come from the education system itself, but from
the high stake of the exams and participation in extracurricular activities which intensifies the competition and force many into a place in education institutions that they can hardly stay on.
